name: governance_attacks
description: Flash-loan-exploitable governance voting from using live token balances instead of historical snapshots
question: The source file in `source` contains a governance/voting contract whose vote-casting or quorum logic determines voting power or quorum using the current token balance (e.g., balanceOf) or current totalSupply() at the time of voting, rather than a historical snapshot taken at proposal creation (e.g., getPastVotes/getPastTotalSupply with a recorded snapshot block), such that tokens acquired and returned within a single transaction (e.g., via flash loan) can be used to cast or swing a vote.
criteria: Voting power is read via token.balanceOf(msg.sender) or an equivalent live balance instead of a checkpointed/historical balance
No snapshot block number or votingDelay is recorded at proposal creation to separate token acquisition from voting eligibility
Quorum or vote totals are computed from totalSupply() at vote time instead of a historical getPastTotalSupply(snapshot)
Delegation and voting can occur within the same transaction without any checkpoint restricting same-block delegated power
No mechanism (getPastVotes, snapshot, or minimum holding period) prevents momentarily-held tokens from being used to vote
